versions.name: RXV2-0.9.607-dongle-rx-only
versions.notes: Dongle: the receiver-only pages (output protocol, bind, receiver settings, diagnostics, simulator, flight records, channel map, fly) show a one-line 'Not on a dongle' note with a Home button instead of their controls, and Find a setting leaves them out of its results (Malcolm 2026-09-10: 'protocol selection not needed for dongle'). Includes 0.9.606.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.606-dongle-banner-quiet
versions.notes: Dongle home page: the wiring hint under the banner shows only while no flight controller answers; once connected the banner is just its title (Malcolm 2026-09-10). Includes 0.9.605.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.605-dongle-banner
versions.notes: Dongle home page: the banner now says the one thing a newcomer needs - 'Connect dongle to a spare UART and use configurator to set that port to MSP 115200' (Malcolm 2026-09-10). Includes 0.9.604.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.604-first-paint
versions.notes: Home page: no more flash of the wrong layout while the receiver answers (Malcolm 2026-09-10). The page remembers what it showed last time - dongle or receiver buttons, the model's name, the version in the footer - and paints that first; the live answer then changes only what differs. The subtitle stays blank instead of saying 'loading'. Includes 0.9.603.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.603-less-words
versions.notes: Fewer words (Malcolm 2026-09-10: 'keep things simple, avoid stating the obvious'): Copy a bank loses its idle 'Ready' box and its introduction; the Easy tuning and Dongle pages lose theirs; on every Rotorflight page the banner appears only when there is something to say - no more 'Loaded from flight controller' after every read (a recorded session still says it came from the phone). Includes 0.9.602.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.602-dongle-no-telem-speed
versions.notes: Dongle: the telemetry speed card (fast / standard) is never offered - the 3-second refresh of the Rotorflight page had been drawing it after the first paint - and the receiver refuses the request from a dongle: the telemetry link speed belongs to whatever receiver flies the model (Malcolm 2026-09-10: 'Not applied' after Apply fast telemetry on a dongle). Includes 0.9.601.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.601-telem-why
versions.notes: Telemetry speed: when the flight controller does not take the new setup, the message and the event log now say which step failed (no acknowledgement, a rejected write, a short read-back, or the byte that came back different). Malcolm 2026-09-10: 'Not applied' with no reason. Includes 0.9.600.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.600-update-pill-tap
versions.notes: Updates page: the amber 'Update available' status pill now doubles as the install button, and says so (Malcolm 2026-09-10: 'I instinctively pressed it'). The note below it was already tappable. Includes 0.9.599.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.599-dongle-identity
versions.notes: Dongle: a phone that connects the moment the board is plugged in no longer starves the flight-controller identity probe (the probe's hold-off after phone traffic is a CRSF-link measure and is skipped on a dongle), and any reply from the flight controller marks it connected at once, so the Rotorflight button appears and the arming watch starts straight away (Malcolm 2026-09-10: 'Dongles 3 and 4 do not show the Rotorflight option'). Receivers unchanged. Includes 0.9.598.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.598-ble-forensics
versions.notes: Dongle Bluetooth forensics (Malcolm 2026-09-10, twice 'not advertising until I rebooted it'): state.json's ble block now names the connected phone (address, connected-for and silent-for times); a dongle keeps its event log through a power-cycle (persisted on every connect/disconnect and every 5 minutes, disarmed only); a dongle drops a silent app after 3 minutes (receiver: 10) so another phone can connect; with nobody connected for 10 minutes the advertising is re-keyed. Receivers unchanged in flight: nothing runs while a transmitter link is live. Includes 0.9.597.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.597-hsi-labels
versions.notes: PIDs page: the row that was called 'HSI off' is the O gain (how strongly the high-speed trim builds up) and is now labelled 'HSI gain (O)'; the PID+ page's 'high-speed trim cap (HSI offset limit)' is the ceiling in degrees. Both help texts now point at each other (Malcolm 2026-09-10: 'their values are different, how do they differ?'). Includes 0.9.596.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.596-ble-watchdog-safe
versions.notes: Bluetooth watchdog made flight-safe (Malcolm 2026-09-10: dongle fixes live in the receiver too). On a receiver it stands down whenever a transmitter link is live, pre-flight or in flight; on a dongle whenever the flight controller says armed. Every condition must hold for two consecutive checks (20 s) before it acts. Includes 0.9.595.
